newsitem.title: UK: Labour says won't pay for new British royal yacht.
newsitem.headline: Labour says won't pay for new British royal yacht.

text.p: Britain's opposition Labour Party said on Saturday it would scrap a government pledge to spend 60 million pounds ($100 million) of taxpayers' money on a new royal yacht if it won the forthcoming general election. The Conservative government announced without warning on Wednesday that it would order a new yacht to replace the ageing Britannia but Labour denounced the plan as a bid to win support ahead of the election, which must be held by May 22.
Labour defence spokesman John Reid told BBC television that the party -- which the Conservatives portray as fiscally irresponsible -- would have other, more important priorities.

"We are saying that we will not fund out of public expenditure 60 million pounds for a royal yacht when there are demands such as hospitals, the health service and education which a Labour government will be expected to meet," he said.
Labour, out of power for almost 18 years but well ahead in the opinion polls, has vowed to keep a tight hand on public spending if it wins the election.
Pragmatists say Britain can no longer afford expensive symbols of past glories while traditionalists see the yacht as a priceless advertisement of all that is best about the country.

When Defence Secretary Michael Portillo made the announcement on Wednesday, he said the new vessel would be built in British shipways and called it "a symbol of the nation's pride". Labour was not impressed.
"The government has used this as a political stunt in a vain attempt to bolster its flagging popularity," said a Labour spokesman on Saturday.

The Mail on Sunday newspaper quoted unnamed royal aides as saying the Queen was unhappy about the way in which Portillo had made the announcement because it had dragged the royal family into the pre-election battle.
The Conservatives say they want a replacement for the 44-year-old Britannia -- now on its final voyage -- in time for Queen Elizabeth's Golden Jubilee in 2002.
Lord Ashbourne, the Conservative chairman of the all-party Royal Yacht Parliamentary Group, said he was disappointed.

"It's very sad. But it's not the end of the world. If a Labour government won't cough up the money, it's possible for the yacht to be funded by private money," he said. Britannia, a 6,000-tonne luxurious mini-liner with a crew of 234 and a Royal Marines band on board, is on its way to Hong Kong to mark the handover of the territory to China at the end of June. The yacht will be decommissioned later in the year.

Although the Britannia costs 10 million pounds ($16 million) a year to run, British exporters say the vessel is a unique asset that has helped secure two billion pounds ($3.2 billion) in business orders over the past decade.
